source: Chattaraj & Raj (2026) LLMs Remember First, Forget Last (Table 8, frontier models)
finding: The PI-harder-than-RI result includes current frontier models among the 39. All 39 show RIES above PIES. Frontier PIES still lags RIES for most.
numbers: 39 models, 1B to 2.5T params. GPT-5 RIES 186.4 / PIES 99.2. Claude-4.5-opus 178.4 / 170.3. Gemini-2.5-pro 162.5 / 123.6. o3 185.8 / 76.0. Mean gap 69.5, t(38)=10.71, d=1.73. RIES vs PIES r=0.21, p=0.201.
limits: Claude-4.5-opus nearly closes the gap (8 points). Closed-model sizes are estimates. Same authors, one paradigm: no independent replication found.
agent_relevance: Gap 3 partly closed: holds for GPT-5, o3, Gemini-2.5-pro, much weaker for Claude-4.5-opus. Do not assume PI is always worse at frontier.

source: Chattaraj & Raj (2026) reasoning models vs non-reasoning on PI
finding: Reasoning models do much better on RI but collapse on PI at high update counts. Extra reasoning tokens do not help find the latest version.
numbers: 6 reasoning vs 33 non-reasoning. RI mean 178.0 (SD 12.6) vs 150.3 (SD 18.2), t(37)=3.54, d=1.76. PI accuracy at N=3/10/50/100/200/300: reasoning 99.6/59.1/0/0/0/0; non-reasoning 93.5/69.4/53.6/10.9/9.9/3.4. o1 RIES 186.4 rank 1, PIES 22.0 rank 35 (text says 21.9).
limits: Only 6 reasoning models. Reasoning traces may themselves add similar entries.
agent_relevance: Gap 7 closed for this paradigm: more reasoning does not rescue latest-version lookup. Use explicit supersession or a reset, not more thinking.

source: Wang & Sun (2025) Unable to Forget: mock QA reset and forget-prompt text
finding: The mock QA reset is the one effective fix, but the text gives no table. The only anchor is a comparison. Forget prompt gives under 10 points.
numbers: Gemini Flash 2.0 with the reset, at 150 updates, matched its no-reset accuracy at 30-45 updates. Reset inserted after 120 updates. Per-key forget prompt under 10 points at 100 updates, negative for gpt-4.1-mini. Soft session reset: largely ineffective (figure only). No semantic-similarity ablation. Value length: below 40% at 10 words, below 5% at 40 words.
limits: Equal-token comparison against summarize-and-restart or fresh context was not run. Exact gain still only in a figure.
agent_relevance: Gap 6 stays open for the ranking of resets. One model: reset acts like removing roughly 105 to 120 of 150 stale updates. Gap 9: length is tested only as a driver, never as a fix.

finding: Write-time handling of stale memories (CUPMem) lifts scores far above plain models and memory frameworks. Stale states are archived, not deleted.
numbers: CUPMem on GPT-4o-mini backbone 68.0% overall vs plain GPT-4o-mini 8.7%, Gemini-3.1-pro 55.2%, LightMem 17.8%. Premise resistance 78.0 / 75.0 vs near 0 for most baselines. Context about 151.8K tokens, 50 sessions, 593 turns, 400 scenarios, 1,200 queries. Gemini-3.1-pro State Resolution 92.0 (Type I) to 69.0 (Type II).
limits: No component ablation in the paper (adjudicator, stale marking, replace vs delete). Single context length. CUPMem score is the authors' own system.
agent_relevance: Gap 4: supersession handling is worth tens of points, but STALE does not separate tagging from deleting.

source: Li & Li (2026) What Should an Agent Forget? (ablations)
finding: Leaving older revisions active in the memory view costs 23 to 33 points. Marking the older fact superseded and leaving it out of the view (archive kept) is the key component.
numbers: Budget B=2,048 tokens. Full vs -FORGET: AMB-Text 91.86 vs 68.60; LME-KU 93.59 vs 60.26; MAB-FC 74.00 vs 51.00. -SLOT (no slot grouping) 86.05/89.74/64.00. -RESCUE 88.37/91.03/65.00.
limits: One model (GPT-5.6-Luna). One budget. Not a cap test and no equal-budget sweep. Compares superseded-and-hidden vs left active, not tag-and-keep vs delete.
agent_relevance: Gap 4 mostly closed: hide-superseded-in-view with archive beats keeping all revisions active by 23 to 33 points. Same-slot grouping adds 4 to 10.

source: Lee et al. (2026) MINTEval temporal cues (visible text numbers)
finding: Dates and times on facts and questions shrink the lookback drop. The size is in the text after all, not only in Fig 8.
numbers: Drop from first to last lookback step: Full Context 13.22 to 5.48; RAG 31.43 to 10.45. Distractors 1/3/5 tested: performance falls with count, values only in figure. Out-of-domain distractors hurt RAG most.
limits: bAbI-style synthetic. Fig 8 per-method values and the superseded-removal baseline are not in the text. Average accuracy 27.7 vs 27.9 inconsistency stands.
agent_relevance: Gap 4: timestamps cut the lookback loss by about 59 percent (Full) and 67 percent (RAG) in relative terms, computed here from the two pairs.

source: Nakshatri et al. (2025) When Facts Change (evolveQA, date hint appendix C.3)
finding: A bare date hint generally does not help with evolving facts. Explicit entity-concept-attribute context helps up to about 11 points.
numbers: Open-ended accuracy baseline to date-only: Claude 3.5 Sonnet v2 AWS 26.95 to 28.40, Azure 22.95 to 22.40; GPT-5-mini WHO 50.64 to 46.15. Context-only: Claude 3.5 Sonnet v1 Azure 21.31 to 32.24 (+10.93). Superseding-knowledge MCQ drops: GPT-4.1-mini AWS 62.78 to 47.76 (-15.0). Outdated Response Rate 23 to 55 percent.
limits: Date was sampled relative to model cutoff, not the true current date, so it tests something different from MINTEval cues. Number of prior versions not isolated.
agent_relevance: Gap 4 conflict: tags help when they order versions inside the memory (MINTEval), not when a date is only a hint about the present.

source: Ding et al. (2026) CMI dose-response, lexical retrieval (TravelPlanner)
finding: With lexical retrieval the damage is done by 2 related entries, then flat. There is no gradual knee past 2.
numbers: Plasticity at 0/2/4/8 added: neutral .84/.84/.84/.84; unrelated .84/.84/.82/.82; repeated .84/.50/.50/.50; same-slot .84/.08/.34/.34. 50 base scenarios per cell. Same-slot stability .92/.82/.88/.88.
limits: Counts 0,2,4,8 only; no 1 and no 3. TravelPlanner only. Same-slot at 2 (.08) is lower than at 4 and 8, which looks like noise or a quirk.
agent_relevance: Gap 5 partly closed: a cap near 2 per slot would sit at the knee in this setup. Sparse design, so 3 to 5 is not tested.

source: Ding et al. (2026) CMI dose-response, dense retrieval
finding: With dense retrieval the loss keeps growing with count. Stability falls steadily for same-slot conflict.
numbers: Plasticity 0/2/4/8: unrelated .84/.76/.70/.66; repeated .84/.58/.40/.38; same-slot .84/.60/.44/.40. Same-slot stability .92/.78/.62/.54. Neutral stays .84 to .80. Trained selector IAAR raised noisy-update success .386 to .686 (+.300, 95% CI .129 to .486) in-domain, +.114 on LongMemEval.
limits: No cap, dedup, or supersession arm in this paper. Knee for dense repeated history is around 2 to 4.
agent_relevance: Gap 5: dense knee at 2-4 supports a cap of about 3, but the cap itself is untested. Even unrelated entries cost 18 points at 8 under dense retrieval.

finding: Removing distractors helps small models but adds little for the largest ones. Most of the naive truncation loss is lost signal, not removed interference.
numbers: 25 percent retention, change vs full context. BABILong distractor-aware: Haiku 4.5 +0.083, Sonnet 4.6 +0.104, Opus 4.7 +0.008, GPT-5.5 +0.017. MRCR v2: Haiku +0.198, Sonnet -0.112, Opus -0.060. Naive BABILong Opus 4.7 -0.433, GPT-5.5 -0.613.
limits: Distractors defined structurally, no similarity measure. Opus 4.7 and GPT-5.5 ran at default temperature.
agent_relevance: Gap 10 stays open (no similarity metric). Frontier models gain little from pruning distractors in these tasks, so caps may matter less for them than for mid-size models.

source: Xiong et al. (2025) How Memory Management Impacts LLM Agents (Tables 1 and 2)
finding: Add-all lowers accuracy against a fixed small memory on every agent. Strict selective add beats both. History-based deletion helps on top.
numbers: SR/ACC, add-all vs strict: RegAgent 55.48 vs 70.95; EHRAgent 13.05 vs 38.50; AgentDriver 32.32 vs 51.00; CIC-IoT 59.90 vs 85.40. Fixed memory (100/100/180/50 records): 67.53/16.75/40.11/71.50. Strict+history deletion: EHR 42.06 (784 records), CIC 89.60. Strict+periodic: CIC 80.80 (310 records), RegAgent 67.65 (949). Retained records correct 44.1-54.8% vs deleted 32.1-48.2% (EHR).
limits: Memory sizes are record counts, not token budgets, so not equal-token. No per-class cap arm. No numeric similarity threshold reported (input-output similarity r near 1 for RegAgent).
agent_relevance: Gap 1 stays open: selective add and deletion are tested, a per-class cap is not. Strict add shrinks memory 30 to 60 percent vs add-all while raising accuracy.

source: Decocted Experience (2026) memory consolidation sweet spot
finding: The text says performance peaks at intermediate memory size, above full memory. No numbers in text.
numbers: Defaults: K=8 math, K=4 WebShop, K=4 SWE; leaf sizes 50/20/10. No k sweep numbers.
agent_relevance: Gap 1: directional support that fewer, merged entries can beat full memory. Not a cap test.

source: Roberts et al. (2024) LLM Recall Uncertainty and the Fan Effect
finding: Fan effect in LLMs is weak and model-dependent. Only some models show uncertainty tied to fan.
numbers: Mistral and SOLAR, 50 each, 26 person-place concepts, fan 0 to 3. All 'absent' correlations significant, no 'present' one significant. Noise floors 0.3 to 0.45. Typicality r>0.3 for Mistral and SOLAR only; RoBERTa, GPT-2, Llama-2 none.
limits: Token probabilities not accuracy. Small models. Coefficients only in figures.
agent_relevance: Gap 10: no validated similarity threshold from fan-type work.

source: Kerestecioglu et al. (2026) Human-Inspired Memory Architecture (abstract page numbers)
finding: Dedup-based consolidation shrinks the store with no accuracy loss on a real issue tracker. M-tier budget figures not rechecked.
numbers: VSCode 13K issues, 120K events: 97.2% retention precision, 58% store reduction, +21.8 pp over baseline. LongMemEval 475 sessions at 200K tokens: 70.1 vs 71.2 raw, overlapping 95% CIs. S-tier 50 sessions: preference recall +13.3 pp.
limits: No cap-per-class arm. Thresholds 0.542 and 0.559 not reconfirmed this session.
agent_relevance: Gap 10: a similarity merge is feasible at 58 percent reduction, but no threshold sweep against accuracy.

source: Loftus & Patterson (1975) quoting Keppel & Underwood 1962 Exp 2
finding: Second-hand numbers for PI build-up in short-term recall, plus the design used to show release by category change.
numbers: Keppel & Underwood (1962, Exp 2): asymptote of the retention curve .99 on Trial 1, .58 on Trial 3. Loftus & Patterson: 24 trials in 8 blocks of 3, new taxonomic category per block, 15 s retention.
limits: Quoted second-hand. Original 1962 tables not opened.
agent_relevance: Gap 8 partly closed: PI build-up in 3 trials is about 41 points. Confirms rotate-category-every-3 as a human design.

source: Lindsey (undergraduate thesis, Georgia Tech) Mechanisms of temporal release from PI
finding: Release size depends on how different the new class is. Content change releases more than a time change.
numbers: Initial content release study (Wickens, Born & Allen 1963) release 91%; first time-based release (Kincaid & Wickens 1970) 74%. Fruits to professions releases more than fruits to vegetables (Wickens, Dalezman & Eggemeier 1976). Language and modality shifts also release (Wickens 1970). Accuracy rises with inter-trial interval out to 45 s.
limits: Student thesis summarizing others; year not stated in text. Primary 1963 and 1970 tables not opened. Per-trial percent correct still missing.
agent_relevance: Gap 8 partly closed: release is graded by category distance. Agent rule: shift to a far class, not a neighbor class.

source: Turvey, Cremins & Lombardo (1969) and a 2018 Memory study (search snippets only)
finding: Snippets: Turvey et al. report release at 5 s and 15 s after a class shift at Trial 4, favouring an interference reading. A 2018 study found intervening new-category trials neither reduced nor released PI.
agent_relevance: Boundary condition: release is not guaranteed by any category change. Check before relying on it.

source: Associative Interference-aware Memory, AIM (ICLR 2026, When Memories Collide)
finding: A training-free agent memory with per-item interference tracking had the best accuracy under memory load. A follow-up on another model found the ledger, not sparse encoding, did the work.
numbers: No numbers on the abstract page. OpenReview id Y7r5ZODl7l.
limits: Abstract only, numbers not read. Domain-shift setting. Tolerance for extra context depends on domain.
agent_relevance: Gap 1: nearest agent-level evidence that tracking interference per item beats keeping everything. Read full paper next.

source: Search status note for gaps 2 and 9
finding: No paper found that tests a category-change release for LLMs as gap 2 asks. Chattaraj lists category shift only as background. No paper found that tests compressing entries as a fix.
numbers: Web search budget ran out. arXiv, OpenAlex and Semantic Scholar APIs returned 429 or no budget, so the sweep for newer papers is incomplete.
limits: Absence of evidence from an incomplete search.
agent_relevance: Gaps 2 and 9 stay open and are cheap to test in-house.
